title: Browser addon: executable lookup and launch flags
answers: How does the browser addon find chrome/firefox per platform?
What flags does the browser addon pass to Chrome?
How does Firefox get proxy config in browser addon?
body:
- Lookup helpers in mitmproxy/addons/browser.py: find_executable_cmd(*paths) returns [path] for first shutil.which hit (absolute or PATH names); find_flatpak_cmd(*ids) needs flatpak, runs `flatpak info <id>`, returns ["flatpak","run","-p",id].
- Each launcher tries native candidates (macOS app path, Windows Program Files paths, then Linux names) and falls back to flatpak. Not found → logs "Your platform is not supported yet" and returns. To support a new platform/browser path, add to the search list in launch_chrome/launch_firefox.
- Chrome (launch_chrome): fresh tempfile.TemporaryDirectory as --user-data-dir, --proxy-server=<listen_host or 127.0.0.1>:<listen_port or 8080> from ctx.options, --disable-fre, --no-default-browser-check, --no-first-run, --disable-extensions, about:blank.
- Firefox (launch_firefox): no proxy flag; writes prefs.js into temp profile (network.proxy.type=1, http/ssl host+port loop), launches `--profile <tmp> --new-window about:blank`.
- Gotcha: missing comma between app.shield.optoutstudies.enabled and extensions.blocklist.enabled prefs merges them into one string; prefs are written without newlines via writelines. Apparently still works.
- stdout/stderr go to DEVNULL.
